title: 2011 AMC 10A Problem 22
statement: Each vertex of convex pentagon \(ABCDE\) is to be assigned a color. There are \(6\) colors to choose from, and the ends of each diagonal must have different colors. How many different colorings are possible?

solutions.text:
Note that there are only \(3\) cases: all the vertices are different, there is one pair of adjacent vertices with the same colors, or there are \(2\) pairs (each pair has a different color).

Case \(1:\) all vertices have different colors

This case just gives us \(6! = 720\) different colorings.

Case \(2:\) one pair of adjacent vertices has the same color

There are \[ \dfrac{6!}{2} = 360 \] ways to choose the colors for this case. There are then \(5\) options for the pair of vertices.

This gives us a total of \[ 360 \cdot 5 = 1800 \] colorings for this case.

Case \(3:\) two pairs of adjacent vertices have the same color

There are \(5\) choices for the vertex that is not in a pair. There are then \[ 6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 = 120 \] choices for the colors. There are then a total of \[ 120 \cdot 5 = 600 \] colorings for this case.

There are a total of \[ 720 + 1800 + 600 = 3120 \] colorings for all the cases.

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Case on whether \(5\), \(4\), or \(3\) colors are used
Repeated colors can occur only on adjacent vertices
